flavor.phonemic_palette: Mongol-Turkic backbone (vowel harmony; kh, gh, ch, sh, ng, q; -ai/-tai/-chi) with a Sinitic overlay (monosyllabic Chinese loanwords in the bureaucratic register, -cheng/-shan toponyms, court titles); theophoric on the Steppe morphs (Marakhai-, Tulai-) with Sinitic variants (Maluo-, Tuli-).
flavor.phenotype_notes: Synthesis of Chinese + Steppe-Mongol per setting-lore §5.3 (blend the listed features; exclude the inverse).

magic_attitude.notes: Chinese + Steppe-Mongol register; deity-morphs in name_bank 'xiongan'.

religion_hooks.alignment_lens: Resolved per the culture's chosen alignment (setting-lore §4.2): Lawful venerates the 12 Lawful powers and names the 13 as demons; Chaotic venerates the 13 and names the 12 as tyrant-gods; Neutral venerates this culture's ancestral saints, invoking the great gods only situationally.

flavor_text.one_line: Xiongan — tolerant imperial bureaucracy of the plains; strength, glory.
flavor_text.one_paragraph: The Xiongan (Chinese + Steppe-Mongol) are a expansionist imperial bureaucracy people seeded in plains, hills, mountains. They prize strength, glory, law, lean toward the military sphere, and field horse_archers, heavy_cavalry, crossbowmen. Outsiders are met as tolerant; their patrons touch war, storms, trade.
